architecture: System follows a polling architecture driven by a real-time timer interrupt.
Data Flow: Timer Tick -> Sensor Driver (ADC) -> Digital Filter -> Unit Conversion -> Threshold Comparator -> Alert Handler -> I/O Output.
Control Loop: Non-blocking main loop handles I/O, Timer ISR handles sampling.

components.name: Sensor Interface Driver
components.role: Reads raw ADC values or I2C/SPI data.

components.name: State Machine
components.role: Tracks Normal, Warning, Fault, Sensor_Error states.

components.name: Alert Reporter
components.role: Writes to Serial Log or toggles GPIO pin.

fault_detection.logic: Transition to Warning/Fault requires 3 consecutive samples out of range.
fault_detection.rationale: Prevents transient noise spikes from triggering false alerts.

fault_detection.logic: Raw ADC value out of [0, 4095] range (assuming 12-bit) -> Flag SENSOR_FAIL.

assumptions: Sensor provides linear output over 0-100°C range mapped to ADC 0-4095.
Communication bus (I2C/ADC) does not experience sustained corruption.
Human operator monitors logs within 1 minute of alert.
System clock source is accurate enough for 1% timing variance.
risks: Sensor wiring loose -> reads 0V -> False Fault <0°C.
ADC Reference voltage drifts -> Systematic calibration error.
High electromagnetic interference -> Single sample spikes -> False Warning.
Buffer overflow -> Log file truncates old alerts.
